subject: A gray tabby cat curled up asleep on a folded yellow knitted blanket, on a wooden windowsill beside a sunny window
focal_point: The cat's sleeping face: the closed eyes, the pink nose, the white muzzle with its whiskers and the two white paws tucked under it
light: Daylight comes through the window at the upper left. It lays warm peach patches on the sill at the left, lights the top of the cat's head, back and tail and the tops of the blanket's rolls, and leaves the cat's belly, the right end of the blanket and the front of the sill in shadow.
why: Start with the farthest things, the sky and trees seen through the window, then the plain blue-gray wall painted straight through where the cat will lie, the white window frame over the join, and the wooden sill. The yellow blanket goes in next, finished with its knit marks, so the cat can be laid on top of it; the cat then gets most of the steps, built the way a teacher builds an animal: a gray shape, its shadow, the white patches, the stripes, two passes of fur, and the face last, ending on the whiskers.

things.name: The sky through the window
things.why: A small patch of clear sky, bluer at the top and paler toward the trees: one wet blend.

things.name: The leafy trees outside
things.why: A soft mass of leaves seen through the glass: dark dabs, then a few sunlit dabs.
things.left_out: Single trees, trunks and branches, and a middle green: the trees are only a dabbed mass of dark and sunlit green.

things.name: The blue-gray wall
things.why: A plain wall that goes from a paler blue-gray at the top to a slightly deeper one lower down, laid wet in one go with criss-cross strokes; no wall element exists, and a blended background is the closest fit.

things.name: The white window frame and ledge
things.why: Simple flat pieces (the upright post, the crossbar, the ledge) with a cool shadow side, built from rectangles.
things.left_out: Moldings and the hardware of the window; the frame is flat cream pieces with one shadow side.

things.name: The wooden windowsill
things.why: A long wooden plank with a dark front edge and sunlit patches; shaped-object is the closest fit, though it has no level horizontal stroke, so the plank is built as a long rectangle in pieces.
things.left_out: Wood grain; the sill is flat red-brown with a dark edge and peach sun patches.

things.name: The yellow knitted blanket
things.why: Two rolled folds of blanket built as long flattened ovals, shaded in the fold and underneath, with the knit shown as rows of comma-shaped stitches in a dark pass and then a light pass.
things.left_out: The real cable-knit pattern: the knit is only suggested with rows of V-shaped comma stitches.

things.name: The sleeping tabby cat
things.why: A short-haired cat with tabby stripes and white patches: exactly what this element builds, shape, shadow, pale patches, markings, fur, face.
things.left_out: Single hairs, the fur tufts inside the ears, and any highlight on the closed eyelids; the fur is two passes of short flicks.

steps.name: Blend the sky in the window

lays.what: the whole window opening at the left edge, from the top of the canvas down to the window ledge: clear sky blue at the top, paler toward the bottom, straight through where the trees and the frame's crossbar will go

steps.after: A strip down the left side of the canvas, about a sixth of its width, is smooth sky, clear blue at the top fading to a pale blue lower down. The rest of the canvas is bare white.
steps.why: The sky beyond the window is the farthest thing in the picture, so it goes on first. Tell the painter here that the light comes from this window, at the upper left.

steps.name: Dab the dark trees

lays.what: the dark leaf mass in the window: soft clumps rising up the left edge and into the lower part of the window, with sky showing between the clumps

steps.after: Over the dry sky, dark teal-green dabbed clumps fill the lower two-thirds of the window strip and climb the left edge, with blue sky showing through the gaps and above them. The rest of the canvas is still white.

steps.name: Dab the sunlit leaves

lays.what: light yellow-green taps on the tops and left sides of the clumps

steps.after: The tops of the tree clumps catch yellow-green light, covering less than the dark; the dark green still shows underneath and lower down in each clump. The window view is done; the rest of the canvas is white.

stages.name: The wall and the window frame

steps.name: Blend the blue-gray wall

lays.what: the whole wall right of the window, from the top edge down to about two-thirds of the way down the canvas, straight through where the cat and the blanket will lie: paler at the top, a little deeper and bluer lower down

steps.after: Everything right of the window is a soft blue-gray wall with visible criss-cross strokes, lighter at the top and a little deeper near its bottom edge, running behind where the cat will go. The window view is at the left; the bottom third of the canvas is still white.

steps.name: Block in the white window frame

lays.what: the frame pieces in cream white: first the tall upright post between the window and the wall, then the crossbar across the upper window, then the deep ledge along the bottom of the window

steps.after: A cream-white window frame now stands over the join of view and wall: a wide upright post, a crossbar across the sky a third of the way down, and a ledge at the bottom of the window. Sky and trees show in the panes; the frame is flat with no shadow yet.

steps.name: Shade the window frame

lays.what: the shadow side of the frame: the inner face of the upright post toward the wall, the underside of the crossbar, the thin edge between the panes and the front face of the ledge

steps.after: The frame now has depth: periwinkle blue-gray strips down the inner side of the post, under the crossbar and along the front of the ledge, with the cream white still showing on the faces toward the light.

steps.name: Block in the wooden sill

lays.what: the whole sill across the bottom third of the canvas, edge to edge, from the window ledge and wall down to the bottom edge, straight through where the blanket will go

steps.after: The bottom third of the canvas is a flat warm red-brown sill, built as one long band, meeting the wall and the window ledge. No white canvas is left anywhere.

steps.name: Shade the sill's front edge

lays.what: a dark band along the front edge at the bottom of the canvas, and a dark shadow band where the blanket's bottom edge and right end will sit

steps.after: A dark chestnut strip runs along the bottom of the canvas and a dark band lies across the middle of the sill where the blanket will rest. The rest of the sill is still the flat red-brown.

steps.name: Lay the sun patches on the sill

lays.what: warm peach sun patches on the left part of the sill, below the window, as slanting rectangles with strips of the red-brown left between them as the shadows of the window bars

steps.after: The left quarter of the sill glows with slanting peach patches of sunlight, split by red-brown strips where the window bars cast shadow. The right of the sill stays red-brown. Wall, window and sill are done; the space for the blanket and cat is still wall and sill color.

steps.name: Block in the yellow blanket

lays.what: the folded blanket in golden yellow: a long flattened oval for the back roll running across the middle of the canvas, then a second rounder roll in front of it, rounded at both ends, over the sill's dark band; straight through where the cat will lie

steps.after: A big golden-yellow blanket shape sits on the sill, from near the window ledge to the right edge, made of two long rolls one in front of the other, flat yellow with no shading or knit yet. It covers the lower wall and the middle of the sill.
steps.why: The cat lies on the blanket, so the blanket is finished before the cat is laid over it. Mention here that the painting goes through an ugly stage around now, and that's normal.

steps.name: Shade the blanket's folds

lays.what: deep ochre along the groove between the two rolls, along the bottom of each roll, at the right end away from the light, and across the top of the back roll where the cat's body will press into it

steps.after: The blanket now looks rolled: dark ochre curves run along the fold between the rolls, under each roll and at the right end, with the golden yellow left on the tops and the left side facing the window.

steps.name: Press in the dark knit stitches

lays.what: rows of small V-shaped pairs of comma stitches in deep ochre, following the curve of each roll, over the whole blanket

steps.after: Rows of dark V-shaped stitches now curve along both rolls, so the blanket reads as knitted. The golden yellow shows between the stitches; the shaded folds are still darkest.

steps.name: Press in the light knit stitches

lays.what: fewer, lighter V stitches in pale butter yellow on the tops of the rolls and on the left side facing the window

steps.after: Pale yellow stitches catch the light along the top of each roll and on the left, covering less than the dark stitches, which still show between them and fill the shaded folds. The blanket is done.

steps.name: Block in the gray cat

lays.what: the whole cat in mid gray: one big oval for the curled body over the right two-thirds of the blanket, then the head as a circle at its left end resting on the blanket, two triangle ears, and the tail as a long curve wrapping along the front of the body; strokes follow the way the fur lies

steps.after: A flat mid-gray cat shape lies curled on the blanket: a big rounded body, a round head at the left with two pointed ears, and a tail curving along the front. It covers the wall above the blanket and the top of the back roll. No shading, white or stripes yet.

steps.name: Shade the cat's shadow side

lays.what: dark gray curved along the lower belly above the tail, the far right end of the body, the underside of the tail, under the chin, and the dip where the head meets the body

steps.after: The cat looks round: dark slate gray curves along its underside, the right end and under the head and tail, with the mid gray left across the top of the back and the head.

steps.name: Paint the white patches

lays.what: the first thin coat of the pale fur: the white muzzle and chin, the white chest patch on the side of the body, and the two front paws tucked over the blanket

steps.after: A thin coat of cream white covers the muzzle, the chest patch in the middle of the body and the two paws, with a little gray still showing through. The rest of the cat is gray and dark gray.

steps.name: Brighten the white patches

lays.what: a second, smaller coat of bright white on the tops of the paws, the upper muzzle and the upper part of the chest patch

steps.after: The white patches are now solid: bright white on the paw tops, the upper muzzle and the top of the chest patch, with the cream white left on their lower, shaded edges.

steps.name: Pull the dark tabby stripes

lays.what: charcoal stripes curving around the body and over the back, bands around the tail, short stripes on the forehead and cheeks, and the dark edges of the ears

steps.after: The cat is now a tabby: tapered charcoal stripes wrap around the body and back, rings band the tail, and short stripes mark the forehead and cheeks, with gray between them. The white patches and ear insides are untouched.

steps.name: Paint the pink insides of the ears

lays.what: the inside of both ears in rose pink

steps.after: Both ears now have dusty pink insides, framed by a gray and charcoal rim. The face still has no eyes or nose.

steps.name: Flick in the light gray fur

lays.what: short flicks of light gray over the whole body, head and tail, across the edges of the stripes, following the way the fur lies

steps.after: The cat looks furry: short light gray flicks break up the flat gray and feather the edges of the stripes, with the darker gray and charcoal showing between them, most of all on the shadow side.

steps.name: Flick the sunlit fur

lays.what: fewer, paler flicks only where the window light hits: silver on the top of the back, the top of the tail and the ear rims, and warm peach on the crown of the head between the ears

steps.after: The top of the cat catches the light: silver flicks along the back and tail and a warm peach glow on the crown, covering less than the first flicks, which still show below them. The face has no features yet.

steps.name: Line the closed eyes and mouth

lays.what: two curved charcoal lines for the closed eyes, a short mouth line under the nose spot, and the thin lines between the toes of both paws

steps.after: The cat is asleep: two soft downward-curving charcoal lines close its eyes, a small mouth line sits on the white muzzle, and fine lines split each paw into toes. The nose spot is still white.

steps.name: Press in the pink nose

lays.what: a small rounded triangle of rose pink for the nose on the white muzzle, above the mouth line

steps.after: A small pink nose now sits in the middle of the white muzzle, above the mouth. Only the whiskers are missing.

steps.name: Pull out the whiskers

lays.what: a few long, thin bright white whiskers fanning out from each side of the muzzle, some crossing the gray cheek and the blanket, and two or three above the eye

steps.after: The finished painting: fine white whiskers fan out from the muzzle across the cheek and onto the blanket, the last bright touch on the sleeping cat's face.
steps.why: The whiskers are the brightest, finest marks and lie over everything, so they come last.
